Homeowners compare a TV media wall to a feature wall from a furniture store. The difference is fit: ours is designed to your wall's exact width, your ceiling height and your equipment list.

How we build a TV media wall

A media wall is not a TV hung on a decorated wall. We design the whole composition first: screen size and viewing distance, panel layout, cabinet depth for your equipment, and where every cable runs. The wall is then built in layers - framing and backing, panel or tile finish, cabinetry, lighting - so the finished wall looks like furniture, not construction. Sound equipment, consoles and routers disappear behind flush panels with ventilation, and the screen sits at the exact height for your seating.

From photo to finished wall

STEP 1 - DESIGN PREVIEW

You send a photo of your room. We design the wall around your space, screen and equipment, and send back a concept with a written estimate.

STEP 2 - MATERIALS & SCHEDULE

You approve the design and materials. We order everything and schedule the build days - most materials are prepared before we arrive.

STEP 3 - BUILD

Our crew builds the wall in layers: framing, finish, cabinetry, lighting and equipment. The room is protected and the site is cleaned daily.

STEP 4 - WALKTHROUGH

We mount and connect the equipment, test lighting and remotes with you, and walk every seam and edge together before final payment.

Send us the photo, get the design and the number in writing, then decide. That is how most of our Alhambra projects start.

What Alhambra clients ask us

How much does a TV media wall cost in Alhambra?

In Alhambra a full media wall starts at $7,500. Where a project lands depends on width, finish and how much cabinetry you want - most of our Alhambra builds finish between $8,000 and $14,000. The design preview is free, and the estimate that follows is itemized and fixed.

How long does a media wall installation take in Alhambra?

Plan on 3 to 5 working days in your home for a full media wall in Alhambra. Everything that can be built or prepared beforehand is - the on-site phase is assembly, finishing and connection, not fabrication.

Can you hide all the wires and equipment?

That is the point of the build. Cables run inside the wall, equipment sits in ventilated bays behind flush panels, and you keep full access through hidden doors - nothing dangles and nothing overheats.
